stimulus.markdown:
A regional juice company sells three flavours, Mango, Guava and Litchi, at four riverside kiosks named P, Q, R and S. Table 1 gives the number of bottles sold and Table 2 gives the selling price of each bottle. All bottle counts are in thousands of bottles; all prices are in rupees per bottle; revenue = bottles sold x price per bottle, so each revenue figure comes out in thousands of rupees.

Table 1: Bottles sold (in thousands)

| Flavour | P | Q | R | S |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Mango | 12 | 8 | 10 | 6 |
| Guava | 5 | 9 | 7 | 4 |
| Litchi | 8 | 6 | 5 | 9 |

Table 2: Price per bottle (in rupees)

| Flavour | P | Q | R | S |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Mango | 25 | 25 | 30 | 30 |
| Guava | 20 | 20 | 20 | 20 |
| Litchi | 15 | 15 | 10 | 10 |

question_text: **How many bottles in total (in thousands) were sold at kiosk Q across all three flavours?**
explanation: Kiosk Q is the second data column: Mango 8, Guava 9 and Litchi 6 bottles, all in thousands. Adding the column gives 8 + 9 + 6 = 23 thousand bottles. The 21 trap drops the 8, the 22 trap misreads Guava as 8, and the 24 trap adds an extra unit.

question_text: **What was the total revenue (in thousands of rupees) generated by kiosk P?**

question_text: **In how many of the twelve flavour-kiosk cells did the revenue exceed 150 thousand rupees?**
explanation: Cell revenues in thousands are Mango 300, 200, 300, 180; Guava 100, 180, 140, 80; Litchi 120, 90, 50, 90. Those above 150 are the four Mango cells plus Guava at kiosk Q (180), giving 5 cells. The 4 trap forgets the Guava cell, while 6 and 3 miscount the Mango row.

stimulus.markdown: The grouped bar chart below shows the number of units sold by three solar lamp models, Solaris, Lumen and Vireo, in the years 2022, 2023 and 2024. All figures are in thousands of units, so a bar of height 40 means 40 thousand units were sold.

question_text: **How many units in total (in thousands) were sold across all three models in 2023?**
explanation: The 2023 bars read 50 for Solaris, 40 for Lumen and 30 for Vireo, all in thousands of units. Their sum is 50 + 40 + 30 = 120 thousand. The 110 trap drops a Vireo unit, 130 borrows a 2024 bar, and 115 comes from misreading Solaris as 45.

stimulus.markdown: The grouped bar chart below shows the number of units sold by three solar lamp models, Solaris, Lumen and Vireo, in the years 2022, 2023 and 2024. All figures are in thousands of units, so a bar of height 40 means 40 thousand units were sold.

question_text: **By what percentage did the units sold of Solaris grow from 2022 to 2024?**
explanation: Solaris rose from 40 thousand units in 2022 to 60 thousand in 2024, an increase of 20 thousand. As a percentage of the 2022 base, 20 / 40 = 50 percent. The 33 trap wrongly uses 60 as the base, 20 is the raw increase read as a percentage, and 40 mixes up the models.

stimulus.markdown: The grouped bar chart below shows the number of units sold by three solar lamp models, Solaris, Lumen and Vireo, in the years 2022, 2023 and 2024. All figures are in thousands of units, so a bar of height 40 means 40 thousand units were sold.

question_text: **In which year were the total units sold across all three models the highest?**
explanation: Year totals in thousands are 40 + 30 + 20 = 90 for 2022, 50 + 40 + 30 = 120 for 2023 and 60 + 50 + 40 = 150 for 2024. The largest total, 150 thousand, belongs to 2024. Because 150 clearly beats 120, the years are not tied and neither earlier year leads.

stimulus.markdown: The grouped bar chart below shows the number of units sold by three solar lamp models, Solaris, Lumen and Vireo, in the years 2022, 2023 and 2024. All figures are in thousands of units, so a bar of height 40 means 40 thousand units were sold.

question_text: **What is the ratio of Lumen units sold in 2024 to Vireo units sold in 2022?**
explanation: Lumen sold 50 thousand units in 2024 and Vireo sold 20 thousand units in 2022. The ratio 50 : 20 divides by 10 to give 5 : 2. The 2 : 1 and 5 : 3 traps come from misreading one of the bars, and 3 : 1 wrongly pairs Lumen with a 2023 Vireo value.

verification.expr: from fractions import Fraction; f=Fraction(50,20); '1' if f==Fraction(5,2) else '0'

question_text: **What was the average number of units (in thousands) sold per model in 2024?**
